args.title: deviation-analysis-memo.docx
args.body:
DEVIATION ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet — Lender Markup Review

TO:      Deal Partner / Client Working Group
FROM:    Banking & Finance Associate
RE:      Counterparty (Lender) Markup — Deviation Analysis vs. Original Term Sheet
DATE:    [Engagement Date]
MATTER:  Banking-Finance — Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet
OUTPUT:  deviation-analysis-memo.docx

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

This memorandum compares the lender’s markup of the Senior Secured Credit Facility term sheet against the original (base) term sheet, reconciled to (i) the disclosure schedules and exhibits, (ii) the controlling partner instructions in the deal-team correspondence, and (iii) the economic / risk allocation implications of the disclosed financial and liability data.

The lender’s markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations:

  1. Indemnification: silent reduction of the indemnification cap, and conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
  2. Material Adverse Effect (MAE): new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already at issue in this matter.
  3. Survival / limitation period: a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, in direct conflict with the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Controlling partner instruction (latest message in the deal-team thread; earlier contrary ordering is superseded):

  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket): CLIENT WILL CONCEDE.
  • Any survival-period reduction: WALK-AWAY ISSUE.

Recommendation at a glance:

  • ACCEPT (per partner instruction): basket conversion to tipping basket.
  • REJECT / WALK-AWAY: shortened survival / limitation period for core representations.
  • REJECT / COUNTER: silent indemnification-cap reduction (and related silent shift of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities).
  • REJECT / COUNTER: MAE regulatory-action carve-outs (especially in light of Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries).

================================================================================
II. MATERIALS REVIEWED
================================================================================

A. Base / original materials
   - Deal materials — banking-finance analyze: Counterparty Markup Deviation Analysis of Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet (Matter File 3) (original term sheet framework; firm-standard representations, warranties, covenants, conditions, indemnification, and termination architecture).

B. Lender / counterparty markup
   - Counterparty markup — banking-finance (lender revision identifying the three deviations described above).

C. Schedules and exhibits (control over general base statements)
   - Schedule 3.7 — two pending regulatory inquiries intersecting the markup’s MAE regulatory carve-outs.
   - Schedule 5.2 — retained liabilities that the markup’s indemnification changes would silently shift.
   - Exhibit B — survival matrix that the markup’s limitation-period change contradicts.
   - Principle: scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base banking-finance materials.

D. Partner instructions (controlling)
   - Deal correspondence — banking-finance: latest partner message revises analysis priorities — concede basket conversion; treat any survival-period reduction as walk-away. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded; only the latest message controls.

E. Playbook / firm posture (applied)
   - Firm banking-finance posture reflected in the base term sheet and Exhibit B survival matrix: maintain deductible (or negotiated) basket structure only where commercially justified; preserve indemnification cap economics; preserve core-rep survival per Exhibit B; resist MAE carve-outs that neutralize known diligence risks.
   - Playbook cross-check: deviations that silently reallocate economics (cap, retained liabilities) or nullify disclosed risk (MAE + Schedule 3.7; survival vs. Exhibit B) are out-of-market relative to firm standard and require express client concession or rejection.

F. Financial / liability data (from schedules)
   - Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities: economic exposure that moves if the indemnification cap is reduced or if basket mechanics change claim-recovery timing and quantum.
   - Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries: non-speculative, currently pending matters; financial and operational impact is precisely the category the lender seeks to carve out of MAE.

G. Excluded
   - Unrelated administrative correspondence misfiled in the matter folder was not relied upon.

================================================================================
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Original term sheet (base / firm standard)
  • Indemnification cap at the negotiated firm-standard level.
  • Basket structured as a deductible (losses borne by the indemnified party until the threshold is exceeded; only excess is recoverable).

Lender markup
  • Indemnification cap is silently reduced (no conspicuous call-out of the quantum change).
  • Basket converted from deductible to tipping basket (once the threshold is hit, losses are recoverable from dollar one).

Schedule / financial cross-reference
  • Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. Under the reduced cap, those retained liabilities are more likely to sit above the recoverable ceiling, silently shifting residual exposure to the client.
  • A tipping basket improves the indemnified party’s recovery mechanics relative to a deductible, but that improvement does not offset a silent cap reduction when Schedule 5.2 liabilities are material to residual risk.

Playbook / partner instruction
  • Partner instruction (controlling): client will CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible → tipping).
  • Partner instruction does not authorize concession of the cap reduction. Silent cap cuts are inconsistent with firm playbook requirements that economic caps be express, quantified, and client-approved.
  • Playbook posture: do not accept silent economic re-trades; require redline visibility and client sign-off on any cap movement.

Risk allocation impact
  • Basket concession: acceptable per partner; limited incremental cost if claim frequency is low, and tipping can be client-favorable if the client is the indemnified party under the relevant regime—confirm directionality against the facility’s indemnity structure before documenting the concession.
  • Cap reduction: adverse. Combined with Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, the reduced ceiling can leave disclosed liabilities unrecoverable. This is a true economic deviation, not a drafting clean-up.

Recommendation — Deviation 1
  • ACCEPT basket conversion (deductible → tipping), expressly per controlling partner instruction; document the concession in the issues list and in the revised term sheet so it is not “silent.”
  • REJECT silent indemnification-cap reduction. Counter: restore base cap; require any cap movement to be (i) expressly quantified, (ii) justified against Schedule 5.2 retained-liability quantum, and (iii) approved by the client.
  • Require a conforming update so Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain aligned with the restored cap and do not create an uninsured gap.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2 — Material Adverse Effect — Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Original term sheet (base / firm standard)
  • MAE definition without carve-outs that neutralize regulatory actions of the kind under diligence in this matter.

Lender markup
  • MAE definition revised to add carve-outs for regulatory action “of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.”

Schedule / financial cross-reference
  • Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these carve-outs.
  • Because scheduled exceptions control over general base statements, the pending inquiries are live, disclosed risk. Carving the same category out of MAE would allow the lender to disregard a deterioration path that the diligence record already flags.
  • Financial implication: MAE is a draw-stop / default / conditionality lever in a senior secured facility. Nullifying MAE for known regulatory exposure weakens lender conditionality in a way that may be intentional from the lender’s seat, but is unacceptable from the borrower/client protection posture if the client relies on MAE symmetry or on MAE as a negotiated shared standard—and is especially problematic if MAE feeds bring-down, pricing flex, or mandatory prepayment constructs tied to credit deterioration.

Playbook / partner instruction
  • No partner concession on MAE carve-outs.
  • Playbook: MAE carve-outs that map onto disclosed, pending regulatory matters are high-severity deviations; reject or narrowly cabin with express knowledge qualifiers and schedule-specific treatment rather than categorical carve-outs.

Risk allocation impact
  • High. The markup does not merely refine MAE; it disables MAE for the precise risk Schedule 3.7 puts on the table. That is a substantive reallocation of regulatory risk, not a market-standard clarifier.

Recommendation — Deviation 2
  • REJECT the categorical regulatory-action MAE carve-outs.
  • COUNTER options (in descending preference):
      (a) Delete the new carve-outs entirely and retain base MAE;
      (b) If commercially necessary, limit any regulatory carve-out to generally applicable rules changes (not entity-specific inquiries or enforcement), and expressly preserve MAE for Schedule 3.7 matters and any expansion, escalation, or material adverse resolution of those inquiries;
      (c) Address Schedule 3.7 through specific indemnities, reserves, or conditions precedent rather than through MAE erosion.
  • Require bring-down and conditionality language to remain consistent with the restored MAE.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3 — Survival / Limitation Period Shortening for Core Representations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Original term sheet (base / firm standard)
  • Survival for core representations governed by the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Lender markup
  • New limitation period shortens survival for the core representations.

Schedule / exhibit cross-reference
  • Exhibit B sets the survival matrix. The markup’s limitation-period change contradicts Exhibit B.
  • Scheduled / exhibit terms control over general base statements; the deliverable must treat Exhibit B as the operative baseline, not as optional guidance.
  • Shortened survival compresses the window to assert indemnity claims on core reps, which compounds Deviation 1 (cap / basket) by reducing both the time and, if the cap falls, the quantum of recovery.

Playbook / partner instruction
  • Controlling partner instruction: any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue.
  • Earlier deal-team messages that ordered priorities differently are superseded and must not be followed.
  • Playbook: core-rep survival is a fundamental risk-allocation term; unilateral shortening against Exhibit B is out of market for firm precedent on this product.

Risk allocation impact
  • Critical. Survival cuts are often more valuable to the drafting party than headline price. Combined with a reduced cap and MAE neutralization of known regulatory risk, shortened survival would leave the client with a narrow, low-ceiling, time-barred indemnity path on the very reps most likely to be implicated by Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2.

Recommendation — Deviation 3
  • REJECT in full. Per controlling partner instruction, treat as WALK-AWAY if the lender insists.
  • Counter position: restore Exhibit B survival matrix in full for core representations; any non-core survival trims, if discussed at all, must be itemized, client-approved, and must not touch fundamental / core reps.
  • Do not package survival concession with the basket concession; partner has severed those issues.

================================================================================
IV. INTEGRATED RISK PICTURE (MARKUP × SCHEDULES × ECONOMICS)
================================================================================

The three deviations are not independent drafting nits. Read together against the schedules:

  • Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries)
        ↔ MAE regulatory carve-outs (Deviation 2)
        ↔ shortened core-rep survival (Deviation 3)
     Effect: known regulatory risk is removed from MAE and pushed outside a shortened claim window.

  • Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities)
        ↔ silent indemnification-cap reduction (Deviation 1)
        ↔ survival cut (Deviation 3)
     Effect: disclosed retained liabilities face a lower ceiling and a shorter runway.

  • Exhibit B (survival matrix)
        ↔ Deviation 3 directly contradicts the exhibit that controls.

  • Basket conversion (Deviation 1, second prong)
        Alone, this is the one item partner has authorized for concession. It must not be used as leverage to force acceptance of the cap cut, MAE carve-outs, or survival reduction.

Net: the markup silently re-trades risk allocation on the exact exposures the schedules disclose, while offering a basket mechanic the client is prepared to give. Accepting only what partner authorized, and holding the line elsewhere, preserves the original term sheet’s economics and the Exhibit B architecture.

================================================================================
V. PLAYBOOK CONFORMANCE CHECKLIST
================================================================================

Item                                         Base / Playbook        Markup              Disposition
-------------------------------------------- ---------------------- ------------------- ------------------------
Indemnification cap                          Firm-standard level    Silently reduced    REJECT / restore; no silent economic re-trade
Basket structure                             Deductible             Tipping basket      ACCEPT per partner (document expressly)
MAE — regulatory action                      No entity-specific     Carve-outs for      REJECT; protect Sch. 3.7
                                             carve-out for known    “kind at issue”     
                                             matter types                               
Core-rep survival                            Exhibit B matrix       Shortened           REJECT / WALK-AWAY per partner
Schedule 3.7 interaction                     Disclosed inquiries    MAE carve intersects COUNTER: no carve-out for Sch. 3.7
Schedule 5.2 interaction                     Retained liabilities   Cap cut shifts risk COUNTER: align cap to Sch. 5.2
Exhibit B control                            Controls over general  Contradicted        Enforce Exhibit B
Silent vs. express economic changes          Must be express        Silent cap cut      Require conspicuous mark-up
Partner priority (latest controls)           Survival = walk-away;  N/A                 Follow latest only
                                             basket = concede

================================================================================
VI. RECOMMENDED RESPONSE PACKAGE
================================================================================

1. Issues list (for lender counsel)
   a. Survival / limitation period (core reps): REJECT — restore Exhibit B in full. Walk-away if insisted upon.
   b. Indemnification cap: REJECT silent reduction — restore base cap; any movement must be quantified against Schedule 5.2 and client-approved.
   c. MAE regulatory carve-outs: REJECT categorical carve-outs; propose narrow generally-applicable-law carve-out only, with express preservation for Schedule 3.7 matters.
   d. Basket: ACCEPT conversion from deductible to tipping basket, expressly documented.

2. Term sheet mark-back
   • Revert survival language to Exhibit B matrix.
   • Restore indemnification cap quantum; add cross-reference that Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities are sized against the restored cap.
   • Delete or narrowly rewrite MAE regulatory carve-outs as above.
   • Implement tipping-basket language as the sole accepted lender revision on indemnity mechanics.

3. Internal client note
   • Confirm directionality of indemnity (who indemnifies whom under the facility documents) before finalizing the tipping-basket concession language.
   • Reaffirm walk-away authority on survival.
   • No authority to trade survival or cap for basket mechanics.

4. Conditions to signing / commitment
   • Bring-down of Schedule 3.7 with no MAE carve-out for those items.
   • Exhibit B attached and incorporated by reference with controlling effect.
   • Cap and basket figures reflected in a single, conspicuous economic summary table in the term sheet.

================================================================================
VII. CONCLUSION
================================================================================

The lender’s markup is largely confirmatory of firm-standard terms but plants three high-impact deviations at the intersection of indemnification economics, MAE, and survival. The schedules and Exhibit B convert those deviations from abstract drafting points into concrete risk shifts on pending regulatory inquiries and retained liabilities.

Under the controlling partner instruction, we concede only the basket conversion. We reject the silent indemnification-cap reduction and the MAE regulatory carve-outs, and we treat any shortening of core-representation survival as a walk-away issue. The mark-back should restore the original term sheet and Exhibit B on those points, document the basket concession expressly, and keep Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2 aligned with the restored risk architecture.

Respectfully submitted,

Banking & Finance Associate
Eve Litigation — SIMULATED / Law Firm Company (synthetic matter)

================================================================================
END OF MEMORANDUM
================================================================================

DEVIATION ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet — Lender Markup Review

TO:      Deal Partner / Client Working Group
FROM:    Banking & Finance Associate
RE:      Counterparty (Lender) Markup — Deviation Analysis vs. Original Term Sheet
DATE:    [Engagement Date]
MATTER:  Banking-Finance — Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet
OUTPUT:  deviation-analysis-memo.docx

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

This memorandum compares the lender’s markup of the Senior Secured Credit Facility term sheet against the original (base) term sheet, reconciled to (i) the disclosure schedules and exhibits, (ii) the controlling partner instructions in the deal-team correspondence, and (iii) the economic / risk allocation implications of the disclosed financial and liability data.

The lender’s markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations:

  1. Indemnification: silent reduction of the indemnification cap, and conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
  2. Material Adverse Effect (MAE): new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already at issue in this matter.
  3. Survival / limitation period: a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, in direct conflict with the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Controlling partner instruction (latest message in the deal-team thread; earlier contrary ordering is superseded):

  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket): CLIENT WILL CONCEDE.
  • Any survival-period reduction: WALK-AWAY ISSUE.

Recommendation at a glance:

  • ACCEPT (per partner instruction): basket conversion to tipping basket.
  • REJECT / WALK-AWAY: shortened survival / limitation period for core representations.
  • REJECT / COUNTER: silent indemnification-cap reduction (and related silent shift of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities).
  • REJECT / COUNTER: MAE regulatory-action carve-outs (especially in light of Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries).

================================================================================
II. MATERIALS REVIEWED
================================================================================

A. Base / original materials
   - Deal materials — banking-finance analyze: Counterparty Markup Deviation Analysis of Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet (Matter File 3) (original term sheet framework; firm-standard representations, warranties, covenants, conditions, indemnification, and termination architecture).

B. Lender / counterparty markup
   - Counterparty markup — banking-finance (lender revision identifying the three deviations described above).

C. Schedules and exhibits (control over general base statements)
   - Schedule 3.7 — two pending regulatory inquiries intersecting the markup’s MAE regulatory carve-outs.
   - Schedule 5.2 — retained liabilities that the markup’s indemnification changes would silently shift.
   - Exhibit B — survival matrix that the markup’s limitation-period change contradicts.
   - Principle: scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base banking-finance materials.

D. Partner instructions (controlling)
   - Deal correspondence — banking-finance: latest partner message revises analysis priorities — concede basket conversion; treat any survival-period reduction as walk-away. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded; only the latest message controls.

E. Playbook / firm posture (applied)
   - Firm banking-finance posture reflected in the base term sheet and Exhibit B survival matrix: maintain deductible (or negotiated) basket structure only where commercially justified; preserve indemnification cap economics; preserve core-rep survival per Exhibit B; resist MAE carve-outs that neutralize known diligence risks.
   - Playbook cross-check: deviations that silently reallocate economics (cap, retained liabilities) or nullify disclosed risk (MAE + Schedule 3.7; survival vs. Exhibit B) are out-of-market relative to firm standard and require express client concession or rejection.

F. Financial / liability data (from schedules)
   - Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities: economic exposure that moves if the indemnification cap is reduced or if basket mechanics change claim-recovery timing and quantum.
   - Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries: non-speculative, currently pending matters; financial and operational impact is precisely the category the lender seeks to carve out of MAE.

G. Excluded
   - Unrelated administrative correspondence misfiled in the matter folder was not relied upon.

================================================================================
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Original term sheet (base / firm standard)
  • Indemnification cap at the negotiated firm-standard level.
  • Basket structured as a deductible (losses borne by the indemnified party until the threshold is exceeded; only excess is recoverable).

Lender markup
  • Indemnification cap is silently reduced (no conspicuous call-out of the quantum change).
  • Basket converted from deductible to tipping basket (once the threshold is hit, losses are recoverable from dollar one).

Schedule / financial cross-reference
  • Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. Under the reduced cap, those retained liabilities are more likely to sit above the recoverable ceiling, silently shifting residual exposure to the client.
  • A tipping basket improves the indemnified party’s recovery mechanics relative to a deductible, but that improvement does not offset a silent cap reduction when Schedule 5.2 liabilities are material to residual risk.

Playbook / partner instruction
  • Partner instruction (controlling): client will CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible → tipping).
  • Partner instruction does not authorize concession of the cap reduction. Silent cap cuts are inconsistent with firm playbook requirements that economic caps be express, quantified, and client-approved.
  • Playbook posture: do not accept silent economic re-trades; require redline visibility and client sign-off on any cap movement.

Risk allocation impact
  • Basket concession: acceptable per partner; limited incremental cost if claim frequency is low, and tipping can be client-favorable if the client is the indemnified party under the relevant regime—confirm directionality against the facility’s indemnity structure before documenting the concession.
  • Cap reduction: adverse. Combined with Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, the reduced ceiling can leave disclosed liabilities unrecoverable. This is a true economic deviation, not a drafting clean-up.

Recommendation — Deviation 1
  • ACCEPT basket conversion (deductible → tipping), expressly per controlling partner instruction; document the concession in the issues list and in the revised term sheet so it is not “silent.”
  • REJECT silent indemnification-cap reduction. Counter: restore base cap; require any cap movement to be (i) expressly quantified, (ii) justified against Schedule 5.2 retained-liability quantum, and (iii) approved by the client.
  • Require a conforming update so Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain aligned with the restored cap and do not create an uninsured gap.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2 — Material Adverse Effect — Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Original term sheet (base / firm standard)
  • MAE definition without carve-outs that neutralize regulatory actions of the kind under diligence in this matter.

Lender markup
  • MAE definition revised to add carve-outs for regulatory action “of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.”

Schedule / financial cross-reference
  • Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these carve-outs.
  • Because scheduled exceptions control over general base statements, the pending inquiries are live, disclosed risk. Carving the same category out of MAE would allow the lender to disregard a deterioration path that the diligence record already flags.
  • Financial implication: MAE is a draw-stop / default / conditionality lever in a senior secured facility. Nullifying MAE for known regulatory exposure weakens conditionality and reallocates regulatory risk away from the negotiated MAE standard. That is unacceptable where Schedule 3.7 already identifies concrete inquiries; categorical carve-outs would neutralize the precise risk the schedule puts on the table.

Playbook / partner instruction
  • No partner concession on MAE carve-outs.
  • Playbook: MAE carve-outs that map onto disclosed, pending regulatory matters are high-severity deviations; reject or narrowly cabin with express knowledge qualifiers and schedule-specific treatment rather than categorical carve-outs.

Risk allocation impact
  • High. The markup does not merely refine MAE; it disables MAE for the precise risk Schedule 3.7 puts on the table. That is a substantive reallocation of regulatory risk, not a market-standard clarifier.

Recommendation — Deviation 2
  • REJECT the categorical regulatory-action MAE carve-outs.
  • COUNTER options (in descending preference):
      (a) Delete the new carve-outs entirely and retain base MAE;
      (b) If commercially necessary, limit any regulatory carve-out to generally applicable rules changes (not entity-specific inquiries or enforcement), and expressly preserve MAE for Schedule 3.7 matters and any expansion, escalation, or material adverse resolution of those inquiries;
      (c) Address Schedule 3.7 through specific indemnities, reserves, or conditions precedent rather than through MAE erosion.
  • Require bring-down and conditionality language to remain consistent with the restored MAE.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3 — Survival / Limitation Period Shortening for Core Representations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Original term sheet (base / firm standard)
  • Survival for core representations governed by the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Lender markup
  • New limitation period shortens survival for the core representations.

Schedule / exhibit cross-reference
  • Exhibit B sets the survival matrix. The markup’s limitation-period change contradicts Exhibit B.
  • Scheduled / exhibit terms control over general base statements; the deliverable must treat Exhibit B as the operative baseline, not as optional guidance.
  • Shortened survival compresses the window to assert indemnity claims on core reps, which compounds Deviation 1 (cap / basket) by reducing both the time and, if the cap falls, the quantum of recovery.

Playbook / partner instruction
  • Controlling partner instruction: any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue.
  • Earlier deal-team messages that ordered priorities differently are superseded and must not be followed.
  • Playbook: core-rep survival is a fundamental risk-allocation term; unilateral shortening against Exhibit B is out of market for firm precedent on this product.

Risk allocation impact
  • Critical. Survival cuts are often more valuable to the drafting party than headline price. Combined with a reduced cap and MAE neutralization of known regulatory risk, shortened survival would leave the client with a narrow, low-ceiling, time-barred indemnity path on the very reps most likely to be implicated by Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2.

Recommendation — Deviation 3
  • REJECT in full. Per controlling partner instruction, treat as WALK-AWAY if the lender insists.
  • Counter position: restore Exhibit B survival matrix in full for core representations; any non-core survival trims, if discussed at all, must be itemized, client-approved, and must not touch fundamental / core reps.
  • Do not package survival concession with the basket concession; partner has severed those issues.

================================================================================
IV. INTEGRATED RISK PICTURE (MARKUP × SCHEDULES × ECONOMICS)
================================================================================

The three deviations are not independent drafting nits. Read together against the schedules:

  • Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries)
        ↔ MAE regulatory carve-outs (Deviation 2)
        ↔ shortened core-rep survival (Deviation 3)
     Effect: known regulatory risk is removed from MAE and pushed outside a shortened claim window.

  • Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities)
        ↔ silent indemnification-cap reduction (Deviation 1)
        ↔ survival cut (Deviation 3)
     Effect: disclosed retained liabilities face a lower ceiling and a shorter runway.

  • Exhibit B (survival matrix)
        ↔ Deviation 3 directly contradicts the exhibit that controls.

  • Basket conversion (Deviation 1, second prong)
        Alone, this is the one item partner has authorized for concession. It must not be used as leverage to force acceptance of the cap cut, MAE carve-outs, or survival reduction.

Net: the markup silently re-trades risk allocation on the exact exposures the schedules disclose, while offering a basket mechanic the client is prepared to give. Accepting only what partner authorized, and holding the line elsewhere, preserves the original term sheet’s economics and the Exhibit B architecture.

================================================================================
V. PLAYBOOK CONFORMANCE CHECKLIST
================================================================================

Item                                         Base / Playbook        Markup              Disposition
-------------------------------------------- ---------------------- ------------------- ------------------------
Indemnification cap                          Firm-standard level    Silently reduced    REJECT / restore; no silent economic re-trade
Basket structure                             Deductible             Tipping basket      ACCEPT per partner (document expressly)
MAE — regulatory action                      No entity-specific     Carve-outs for      REJECT; protect Sch. 3.7
                                             carve-out for known    “kind at issue”
                                             matter types
Core-rep survival                            Exhibit B matrix       Shortened           REJECT / WALK-AWAY per partner
Schedule 3.7 interaction                     Disclosed inquiries    MAE carve intersects COUNTER: no carve-out for Sch. 3.7
Schedule 5.2 interaction                     Retained liabilities   Cap cut shifts risk COUNTER: align cap to Sch. 5.2
Exhibit B control                            Controls over general  Contradicted        Enforce Exhibit B
Silent vs. express economic changes          Must be express        Silent cap cut      Require conspicuous mark-up
Partner priority (latest controls)           Survival = walk-away;  N/A                 Follow latest only
                                             basket = concede

================================================================================
VI. RECOMMENDED RESPONSE PACKAGE
================================================================================

1. Issues list (for lender counsel)
   a. Survival / limitation period (core reps): REJECT — restore Exhibit B in full. Walk-away if insisted upon.
   b. Indemnification cap: REJECT silent reduction — restore base cap; any movement must be quantified against Schedule 5.2 and client-approved.
   c. MAE regulatory carve-outs: REJECT categorical carve-outs; propose narrow generally-applicable-law carve-out only, with express preservation for Schedule 3.7 matters.
   d. Basket: ACCEPT conversion from deductible to tipping basket, expressly documented.

2. Term sheet mark-back
   • Revert survival language to Exhibit B matrix.
   • Restore indemnification cap quantum; add cross-reference that Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities are sized against the restored cap.
   • Delete or narrowly rewrite MAE regulatory carve-outs as above.
   • Implement tipping-basket language as the sole accepted lender revision on indemnity mechanics.

3. Internal client note
   • Confirm directionality of indemnity (who indemnifies whom under the facility documents) before finalizing the tipping-basket concession language.
   • Reaffirm walk-away authority on survival.
   • No authority to trade survival or cap for basket mechanics.

4. Conditions to signing / commitment
   • Bring-down of Schedule 3.7 with no MAE carve-out for those items.
   • Exhibit B attached and incorporated by reference with controlling effect.
   • Cap and basket figures reflected in a single, conspicuous economic summary table in the term sheet.

================================================================================
VII. CONCLUSION
================================================================================

The lender’s markup is largely confirmatory of firm-standard terms but plants three high-impact deviations at the intersection of indemnification economics, MAE, and survival. The schedules and Exhibit B convert those deviations from abstract drafting points into concrete risk shifts on pending regulatory inquiries and retained liabilities.

Under the controlling partner instruction, we concede only the basket conversion. We reject the silent indemnification-cap reduction and the MAE regulatory carve-outs, and we treat any shortening of core-representation survival as a walk-away issue. The mark-back should restore the original term sheet and Exhibit B on those points, document the basket concession expressly, and keep Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2 aligned with the restored risk architecture.

Respectfully submitted,

Banking & Finance Associate
Eve Litigation — SIMULATED / Law Firm Company (synthetic matter)

================================================================================
END OF MEMORANDUM
================================================================================
